name: Josif
desire: see his brother answer for the valley without being the brother who hanged him
need: to keep his own hands clean of his own blood — to hold the instrument, not be the blade
values: the valley's dead over the law's mercy
blood, and the shame of it
fears: that an acquittal frees Radan back into the world
that he is only a coward using a stranger's tongue
contradictions: loves his brother and is condemning him
reveres the oath yet corrupts it by shading his words
beliefs: the law will fail the dead
some truths only the tongue can carry, and only if someone chooses to carry them
knowledge: what Radan did at the sluice
the double sense of the dialect word
that he is steering his own testimony
constraints: cannot say it plainly without becoming the one who said it

syntax: answers a question with a question or a silence
